transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Blake (Amberwood CTO), Priya Nair (Amberwood Head of ML), Samir Patel (Amberwood Security)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, AE on the account. Rafael from SE is with me. How's your afternoon?
[00:08] Jordan Blake: Hey Maya, thanks, all good. Excited to get into what Redwood offers — we've been looking at quickstart options.
[00:14] Rafael Ortiz: Great — quick agenda: understand your TTFT goals, security constraints, and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private fits best. We'll also talk credits and next steps.
[00:25] Priya Nair: Quick context — we're building an assistant for customer ops, some PII-ish ticket data, low throughput initially but need ~300ms median latency for short responses. We want to prototype fast via self-serve if possible.
[00:42] Samir Patel: And to flag security: SOC2 is must, we need KMS/HSM integration (we use Vault/CloudKMS), SSO, audit logs and data residency controls.
[00:55] Maya Chen: Totally — that's normal for finance. Redwood Hosted supports SOC2 and customer-level audit logs; we also offer Dedicated reserved GPU pools and Private (VPC or on-prem) for strict isolation.
[01:10] Jordan Blake: What's the TTFT for a dev to go from sign-up to first inference? We want to show product folks within a day.
[01:18] Rafael Ortiz: For PLG flows, typical TTFT is under an hour for a basic text generation — with our SDK and sample prompts. If you need a pinned model and VPC connectivity, Dedicated/Private adds more setup time — days to weeks depending on approvals.
[01:33] Priya Nair: So Hosted is fastest but then data retention/custody is the worry. If we ingest ticket data, how is it stored?
[01:42] Maya Chen: By default Hosted keeps short-term request logs for debugging but you can opt-out and enable strict no-retain modes for certain endpoints. We can also provide a Private deployment where logs never leave your VPC. There was a doc I can share.
[01:54] Jordan Blake: Can you just send that? Also, sample flow for free credits — how does that work?
[02:01] Maya Chen: We'll provision sandbox credits — typically $2k-$10k depending on pilot. For Amberwood I suggested $5k credits to run a 2-week prototype. Credits are attached to their sandbox org; engineers can use the API key immediately.
[02:14] Samir Patel: On the KMS piece, does Redwood support bring-your-own-key? We cannot have keys in Redwood control plane.
[02:20] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, we have KMS integrations for BYOK with CloudKMS, AWS KMS, and HSM options for Private installs. For Hosted we support envelope encryption and customer-managed keys for storage at rest. There's an integration flow we can send.
[02:34] [Speaker 1]: Sorry, just to chime in — is there a difference in latency when using customer-managed KMS?
[02:38] Rafael Ortiz: Minimal for tokenization/initialization; the per-request path is independent. Larger impact on latency is model choice, sequence length and batching.
[02:46] Priya Nair: On model choice — can we test open models? We want to control hallucination and cost.
[02:53] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, our catalog includes curated open models and quantized variants. For cost you can leverage quantized models and batching. Rafael: we'll run a perf matrix with your prompt set.
[03:05] Jordan Blake: You mentioned batching — our SLA needs median 300ms for short queries. Does batching hurt that?
[03:12] Maya Chen: It's a balance — continuous batching can improve throughput and cost, but for tight latency SLOs you configure low-latency routing and smaller batch windows. We can set up a Dedicated pool tuned for low-latency.
[03:24] Priya Nair: How quickly can we stand up a Dedicated pool for evaluation?
[03:28] Rafael Ortiz: A dedicated pilot can be provisioned in a few days if you commit to a short reserved capacity. Otherwise we can run a performance sandbox on Hosted with a pinned model to emulate Dedicated.
[03:41] Samir Patel: Compliance checklist — SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs must be captured. Does Redwood support enterprise SSO?
[03:49] Maya Chen: Yes, SAML and OIDC, RBAC at token/route level, long retention logs as an add-on. We'll attach our security deck.
[03:58] Jordan Blake: Any customer references in finance?
[04:02] Maya Chen: We have a couple of fintech customers using Dedicated and VPC deployments; I can share anonymized case notes.
[04:08] [00:04:08] Priya Nair: One more question — how do rollouts work? If we ship and want A/B, can Redwood route traffic across models?
[04:15] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, rollout policies support canary, A/B, auto-fallback to cheaper variants. It is part of Redwood Console.
[04:22] Jordan Blake: Great. Let's talk practical steps. If we sign up now, how do we get the engineers to first token?
[04:28] Maya Chen: Step 1: create org and invite devs, Step 2: provision sandbox credits and sample prompts, Step 3: share SDK snippets + Postman collection. Usually they get to first token in <1 hour.
[04:41] Samir Patel: Will there be a separate environment for security testing?
[04:45] Rafael Ortiz: Yes — we provide a sandbox org isolated from prod; we can create a dedicated sandbox instance with specific retention rules.
[04:52] Jordan Blake: Pricing — can you give rough numbers? We need to present to procurement.
[04:56] Maya Chen: I'll send the price sheet. Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved commit with lower per-token unit cost. We also have add-ons for long log retention and extended SLAs.
[05:06] Priya Nair: For the benchmark, we want 1000 requests at peak, and a 300ms median under 2k tokens. Can you measure tokens / second?
[05:16] Rafael Ortiz: We'll run a benchmark with your prompt set and provide throughput (RPS), p50/p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll include model/quantization settings.
[05:27] Jordan Blake: Are there gotchas for running inference on financial text? Filtering, PII?
[05:33] Samir Patel: We need to ensure no PII is logged and that any outputs are audited.
[05:37] Maya Chen: You can configure no-retain endpoints and redact fields client-side before sending. We also support structured outputs and function-calling to limit free-form generation.
[05:48] [00:05:48] Priya Nair: Would you recommend starting Hosted or going straight to Dedicated? We don't want to overcommit.
[05:55] Rafael Ortiz: Start Hosted sandbox with credits to prove the flow and latency profile. If it meets your SLO, then you can scale to Dedicated for predictable economics. Private is recommended only if policy prevents Hosted usage.
[06:08] Jordan Blake: Ok, that seems pragmatic. For Private/VPC, how long to deploy?
[06:12] Maya Chen: Private VPC deployments vary — typically 2–6 weeks depending on networking approvals and KMS integration. On-prem is longer.
[06:20] [Speaker 2]: quick note: are model weights stored in our account for Private?
[06:24] Rafael Ortiz: In Private, model weights are hosted inside your environment; in Hosted we store weights on Redwood infra but access is controlled and audited.
[06:31] Priya Nair: Any obvious cost levers?
[06:34] Maya Chen: Model selection (quantized vs fp16), truncation strategies, batching, and caching of prefixes. Redwood Optimize recommends profiles automatically.
[06:43] Jordan Blake: Can you demo the SDK quickly? Even a 5-min snippet?
[06:47] Rafael Ortiz: Sure — I'll show a curl and SDK snippet.
[06:51] [00:06:51] Rafael Ortiz: (screen) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -d '{"model":"rw-open-7b-q", "prompt":"Summarize ticket: ..."}' — response streams back. The SDK wraps streaming and function calls.
[07:12] Priya Nair: That looks straightforward — any gotchas with streaming and webhooks?
[07:16] Rafael Ortiz: Webhooks are supported; streaming pushes token deltas. You can also do structured function calls to reduce parsing.
[07:23] Jordan Blake: Let's cover the deliverables and timeline.
[07:26] Maya Chen: Deliverables: quickstart guide + API keys within 24 hours, $5k sandbox credits, perf benchmark within a week, and security pack (SOC2 attestation, KMS integration guide).
[07:40] Samir Patel: We'll send back the compliance questionnaire — interested in BYOK for the pilot.
[07:45] Priya Nair: I'll prepare a small prompt set and sample tickets for the benchmark.
[07:49] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll coordinate on scheduling the benchmark run — Rafael will lead.
[07:54] Jordan Blake: Any blockers from our side? Procurement/contracting?
[07:59] Maya Chen: For sandbox pilot, usually just an MSA with limited terms; Dedicated/Private requires SOW and security review. I'll work with legal if needed.
[08:10] [00:08:10] Priya Nair: One more question — can we pin model versions and roll back easily?
[08:15] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, version pinning and rollout policies are supported in console and API.
[08:21] Jordan Blake: Okay, recap and who does what?
[08:24] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya sends quickstart + pricing + security deck; Rafael runs perf and schedules bench; Amberwood shares prompts and their KMS preference; we'll provision $5k credits.
[08:37] Samir Patel: That works. Also please include the audit log retention options and RBAC guide.
[08:43] Maya Chen: Yes will include.
[08:46] [00:08:46] Jordan Blake: Let's aim to have the bench results by next Wednesday — is that doable?
[08:52] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, I'll plan for that.
[08:55] Priya Nair: Thanks all.
[08:58] Maya Chen: Thanks Amberwood team — we'll follow up with materials and calendar invites for the benchmarking slot.
[09:04] Meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions and minor transcription errors (Redwoood vs Redwood, speaker markers sometimes generic). Links/resources mentioned: https://redwood.ai/docs/quickstart (doc link placeholder), security_deck_redwood_v2.pdf (shared drive link).

End of transcript.
